mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real estate activity (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increased consistently over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a supply-side contraction, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary pressure that the Fed is trying to control, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 increased over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and real GDP (GDPC1) is also below its 12-month moving average, it signals a supply-side weakness that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 both below 12-month moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where both INDPRO and GDPC1 are below their respective 12-month moving averages.
